transcript:
Header: Date/Time: 2026-10-07 16:00 PDT | Duration: 45 minutes | Recording ID: ff-20261007-3847
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Eleanor Kim (CTO, Sable Retail), Sam Brooks (Lead Engineer), Priya Nair (Product)

[00:00] Jordan Park: Alright hello everyone, thanks for joining \u0014 Jordan from Redwood. We're gonna run through the SDK quickstarts, Python and TypeScript, auth, env setup, and show a couple of examples with streaming and embedding calls.
[00:18] Eleanor Kim: Hi hi, thanks. We're especially interested in the quickstarts \u0014 want to make sure our eng team can ramp quickly.
[00:24] Maya Singh: Great, I'll share my screen and start with the Python quickstart. Quick note on environment: Redwood SDK supports pip install redwood-inference, or npm package @redwood/inference for node. We usually recommend using a virtualenv or nvm.
[00:45] Sam Brooks: Quick Q \u0014 auth flow, do you support API key only or SSO for service accounts?
[00:50] Jordan Park: API key is the simplest for dev/proof-of-concept. For enterprise we support SAML SSO + provisioning and you can hook into our private deployment with SSO-backed service accounts. We'll share the SSO docs.
[01:05] Maya Singh: On screen: sample Python snippet.
[01:10] Maya Singh: "from redwood import RedwoodClient\nclient = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])\nresp = client.generate('Summarize this order: ...')" \u0014 simple. For streaming: you call client.stream_create and iterate on chunks.
[01:28] Priya Nair: Do you have examples for TypeScript that show tool calling / structured output?
[01:33] Maya Singh: Yep, show ts example: "import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'\nconst client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })\nconst stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-13b', messages: [...] })" \u0014 then you handle data events.
[01:52] Eleanor Kim: How do you recommend storing keys for our infra? We're on AWS \u0014 KMS/HSM?
[01:58] Jordan Park: For hosted customers, we recommend storing in your secrets manager (Secrets Manager or Parameter Store) and rotating keys. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) we integrate with customer KMS and HSM; we can do customer-managed keys. We'll include the KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[02:18] Sam Brooks: Any env/docker quickstart for running locally? We like reproducible dev environments.
[02:22] Maya Singh: Yes \u0014 we have a docker-compose sample that runs a tiny app that calls the SDK. It sets REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var. There is also a local proxy for simulating network conditions.
[02:35] Jordan Park: One thing to flag: if you plan to move to Dedicated later, you'll want to parameterize model selection and batching configs in your app. We can show a migration guide.
[02:48] Priya Nair: On traction, our timeline is Q4 POC, production in Q1. What sort of bench can we run to validate latency?
[02:55] Maya Singh: We can run a quick benchmark with your sample traffic. For embeddings vs. generation the patterns differ \u0014 we usually test 90/10 gen/emb for commerce search. We'll run a small workload on hosted to start.
[03:12] Eleanor Kim: Security questions: SOC2, ISO, audit logs \u0014 do you provide per-request audit logs?
[03:18] Jordan Park: Yes, we provide audit logs; for Private deployments we can give more retention. SOC2 report is in the security pack.
[03:26] Sam Brooks: How accurate are the streaming latencies? We need sub-200ms per token for small responses.
[03:32] Maya Singh: Depends on model and sequence length; with our optimized runtime and batching we see single-digit token latencies on smaller tails, but realistic avg depends. We'll run a latency test.
[03:45] Eleanor Kim: Any gotchas for TypeScript/Node \u0014 like streaming backpressure or memory leaks?
[03:50] Maya Singh: We recommend using backpressure-aware streams and not buffering entire responses for long contexts. For very large batches use streaming or chunking.
[04:05] Sam Brooks: Can you show the quickstart repo structure?
[04:08] Maya Singh: Sure, I've got the GitHub link up (placeholder: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts). Top-level: python/, typescript/, docker/, benchmarks/, security/. Each has README and minimal app.
[04:25] Jordan Park: Note on models \u0014 we have a catalog of verified open models; for PCI-sensitive workloads customers often pick smaller seq lengths and quantized variants. Also we support routing policies \u0014 e.g., route to cheaper model during low traffic.
[04:40] Priya Nair: Is data retained by Redwood for hosted? We need 90-day retention or optional zero retention.
[04:45] Jordan Park: Hosted default is short retention for telemetry, but you can opt for no retention or dedicated/private where data doesn't leave your VPC. We'll include the retention policy doc.
[04:58] Sam Brooks: A bit of a transcription note \u0014 I saw reference to KV cash in a doc earlier \u0014 I assume you mean KV cache?
[05:03] Maya Singh: Yep, KV cache, sorry for the typo in the doc.
[05:10] -- Demo: Maya walks through the TypeScript quickstart, shows code editing, running local docker, setting REDWOOD_API_KEY.
[08:20] Maya Singh: We're now doing a live demo of streaming. You can see partial tokens arriving. There's a small hiccup due to my home network \u0014 apologies, ignore that.
[12:15] Eleanor Kim: Interruption: our security lead will want a diagram of network flows for private vs hosted. Can you add that?
[12:22] Jordan Park: Absolutely \u0014 deliverable, network diagram and SAML flow.
[12:28] Priya Nair: On pricing \u0014 what does dedicated look like for 3 GPUs reserved?
[12:34] Jordan Park: I'll send a detailed pricing sheet, but ballpark we give committed discounts on monthly reserved capacity. We'll include an example TCO calculation for your traffic profile.
[13:00] Sam Brooks: Are there SDK rate limits? We saw some 429 behaviors in quickstarts before.
[13:05] Maya Singh: There are per-account rate limits; for Dedicated we can configure higher throughput. We also recommend exponential backoff and retry logic in client code.
[13:20] Jordan Park: Recap: we'll send pricing + contract, security pack (SOC2, KMS, network diagram), quickstart repo link, and schedule a technical follow-up to run a benchmark.
[13:32] Eleanor Kim: Sounds good. Who will be the main contacts?
[13:35] Jordan Park: I'll be your AE contact; Maya will run the bench and technical calls. Sam and Eleanor on your side.
[13:42] Priya Nair: Timeline check: can we get initial pricing/security docs by Friday?
[13:45] Jordan Park: Yes \u0014 Friday (2026-10-09).
[13:48] -- Closing small talk, end of recorded portion.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and filler; timestamps approximate. References made to shared artifacts: quickstart repo (github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts), security pack link (to be sent), pricing spreadsheet (to be sent).
